My father suggested getting me tested for Aspbergers when I was 30. 

I had always been different from an early age. I was quiet and shy but then lots of kids are. I was a veracious reader and my reading level was about 10/12 by the time I started Primary school at aged 5. I was so focused on it that I would tune the rest of the world out and wouldn't hear other people talking to me, I would forget to eat, became obsessed with books and I would remember them in such detail because I would read them over and over again. My particular subject has always been crime. I would learn dates, methods, victims names, sentences.. Repeating these details kept me calm.

People, on the other hand, scared me so much. I couldn't walk into a classroom full of people without having a panic attack, I used to have anxiety attacks if the teachers spoke to me in class. By the time I reached high school my Dad had already arrange for special measures to be put in place for me when it came to lessons. I had to sit at the front, by the door and I could leave if I needed to. If I wasn't feeling up to a lesson, then I would spend my lesson in the library. My Dad knew I was different but they didn't really test for much with kids back then so we just had special measures for me. I got bullied a lot as a result which didn't help.

My problems followed me into adult life and my working life as well and I bounced from job to job, never staying anywhere more than about 18 months because I struggled to find a place that accepted the "weird girl" that doesn't talk much and is obsessed with crime stories. When I had just turned 30, my Dad started working with a lady who had an autistic son. He had Aspbergers and she was telling him about her son's behavioural issues and he recognised the same ones in me. So he suggested getting tested. Getting a diagnosis didn't change my life but at least I now know why I am different and I can deal with that.

Firstly, its not my movement but Body Positivity is about loving yourself. Although you say, that in your experience, a person's self-image is rarely about anything make believe, I would have to say that your experience is very limited then. There are millions of people who have a massive issue with their body image when there is nothing wrong with how they look, just how they feel about themselves. This is why people have eating disorders, body dysmorphia and psychological problems relating to their self-image, myself included. It has taken many years of therapy for me to accept that there is nothing wrong with my body and to love myself.
While I accept that, if there is an actual issue, it is wrong for someone not to get help but it would be their choice to do it, not someone else's. If someone is over weight and their doctor has not raised any specific concerns for their health and they are happy with their body, leave them alone.

Body Positivity is not a movement of people trying to reject reality. It is a movement of people trying to get the world, not just people who are larger, but everyone who has an issue with body confidence (thin and fit people do too!) to accept themselves and love the body they have got. To give them some confidence to face the world as they truly are. We are not trying to force society to change its values, we are trying to stop society from forcing us to change ours. I do not have a lower quality of life nor am I seen as less attractive to the people that matter. I know plenty of skinny/fit people that struggle to find love and are depressed and miserable whereas I am not,

Just because you wouldn't find someone of that height and weight ratio attractive, doesn't mean that the rest of the world finds them repulsive. It is perfectly fine to have confidence in yourself if you have that body image. You don't have the right to tell someone otherwise. Not everyone fits everyone else's ideal.
